analysis:
This PR changes documentation only (docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md, docs/reference/configuration.md); no executable code is supplied. docs/reference/configuration.md now describes the following:
- Cluster runtime facts move to schema v2.
- A signed release registers them as `cluster_runtime` in `POST /v1/releases`.
- The coordinator derives approvals, grants and parity qualifications from that block.
- Public declarations (GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B) rest on an owner decision plus an evidence report.
- Qualifications apply family-wide.
- The strict decoder refuses unknown, missing or repeated fields, and a missing grant leaves members held to single-Mac requirements.
I report one low-severity threat-model gap: the release credential and qualification generations (A-005, A-017, T-054) now gate public cluster routing through a path the model does not describe. The Qwen assistant policy is reinforced: a setup with `tensorAssistant` beside `nativeMember` is refused on save and load, and an approval for it is refused before any part stops. Approval fallback now skips coordinator-decided ends and bounds the retry window to 3,600 s, which looks safe for availability. The two-mac-cluster.md changes add an updating section and a Qwen MTP policy table, and mention pair-wide cache sync. I found no regression in the text, but code behaviour is unverified. The next pass should check these points: coordinator-side enforcement of `parityQualification` family-wide application, who may call `POST /v1/releases`, and the `ClusterConfiguration.validate` refusal. Existing pair-wide prompt-cache and T-041 cache behaviour looks unchanged in the docs.

findings.detail: The updated 'Cluster runtime facts' section says a signed release's `POST /v1/releases` payload (`cluster_runtime`) now lets the coordinator derive cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications. It also says a promotable qualification applies to a whole mode family on any numerics classes, cuts and shares. As a result GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B are admitted to public traffic in pipeline and tensor parallel on any Apple silicon pair, on the owner's decision. The text admits that no pipeline of either model ran on two M5 Ultras and that GLM has no TP cross-cable record. This widens what the release credential (A-005) and the build qualifications (A-017) can authorise: a compromised or mistaken release registration could now qualify a model, build and mode family for public routing without separate operator approval. A-005, A-017 and T-054 do not describe this path. Fix: record this derivation path and the decision-based, record-less qualification in the threat model, and state the coordinator-side control that bounds it. The control is outside the supplied evidence.
findings.title: Docs describe release-derived cluster approvals and family-wide public qualification; threat model not updated
